'''Larry Dale Kirkpatrick''' (born February 11, 1941) is an American physicist.

Kirkpatrick was born in the state of Washington in 1941.<ref name="physt"/> He studied physics at [[Washington State University]], graduating in 1963, and pursued a doctorate at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="physt"/><ref name="mtsu">{{cite news |title=Larry Kirkpatrick, Ph.D |url=https://physics.montana.edu/directory/emeritus/kirkpatrick-larry.html |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=Montana State University}}</ref> Upon completing his Ph.D. in 1968, Kirpatrick accepted an assistant professorship at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="physt"/><ref name="mtsu"/> In 1974, he joined the [[Montana State University]] faculty.<ref name="physt"/> He was president of the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]] in 1999.<ref name="physt">{{cite journal |last1=Wheeler |first1=Gerald F. |title=Meet your new president: Larry Kirkpatrick |journal=The Physics Teacher |date=8 April 1999 |volume=37 |issue=2 |page=70 |doi=10.1119/1.880176}}</ref> That same year, Kirkpatrick was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "for exceptional contributions to physics education as textbook author, editor/columnist for [[Quantum Magazine|''Quantum'' magazine]], and as coach of the [[United States Physics Olympiad|US Physics Olympics Team]]."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=K&year=2021&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>
